findings.evidence: Probe: trained a 4096-vocab byte-level BPE with train_tokenizer on generator text (6000 code docs plus facts, reasoning, patterns and fixture prose; scratchpad tokprobe.py). The bench prompt tail is ['."""', 'Ċ']; prompt plus reference gives ['."""', 'ĊĠĠĠ', 'Ġreturn', ...]. For 50/50 function items, the prompt tokens are not a prefix of the prompt+reference tokens. The same alignment check over every other non-chat bench item (reasoning 700 options, pattern 150, knowledge 650, consistency 480, coding outputs 100) found 0 mismatches. In code training text, the token after a bare 'Ċ' was a pure-space token 0 times out of 21,941 (top: print 8999, Output 3001, Ċ 2999, for, def, if). A closing docstring was followed by 'ĊĠĠĠ' 2011/2011 times. I checked the ledger, ADR 0001 and the Task 12/16 reports: there is no ruling on this. The Task 16 fakes are keyed by exact token tuples, so they cannot show it.
findings.fix: Show the model the header without its trailing newline: the item prompt ends at the closing `"""`, so the first generated token is the 'ĊĠĠĠ' it was trained on. Keep check_args['prompt'] (with the newline) for building the MiniPy source; function_body already skips the empty first line of a reply that starts with '\n'. Start the reference with '\n'. Add a test with a trained fixture tokenizer: for every non-chat bench item, tok.encode(prompt) must be a token prefix of tok.encode(prompt + continuation). This must be fixed before bench-v1 freezes.
findings.line: 878 (_Variant.prompt ends with '"""\n'), 1004-1009 (item prompt and check_args prompt), 927 (training text = prompt + body); see also evals/suite.py:151-154 and tokenizer.py:80
findings.scenario:
tok-v1 uses a ByteLevel pre-tokenizer with the GPT-2 regex (tokenizer.py:80). Its `\s+(?!\S)` rule splits the training text `..."""
    return x * 2` into '."""', '
   ' (newline plus 3 spaces), ' return'. BPE merges that first piece into one token (ĊĠĠĠ) because code makes up 1/8 of the tokenizer sample. The bench prompt `def f(x):
    """doc"""
` ends at the end of the string, so its last token is a bare 'Ċ'. suite._prompt_ids feeds encode_doc(prompt) unchanged, with no token healing. In the code training text, a bare 'Ċ' is always followed by a column-0 statement ('print', 'Output', 'def', 'for', 'Ċ') and never by a space token. A closing docstring is always followed by 'ĊĠĠĠ'. So a model that has learned to write bodies still continues at column 0 with greedy decoding, for example `print(add(2, 3))  # 5`. checkers.function_body (checkers.py:152-162) cuts at that first unindented line and returns ''. The source is then the bare def plus docstring, which returns None, so every hidden test fails. This hits all 50 fmt:function items, a third of coding, so the coding category can never go much above about 67% raw, and the 'coding/fam:*' function tags stay near 0 in the frozen bench-v1 whatever the player trains.
findings.title: Function-completion prompts end on a lone newline token that training never puts before a function body, so all 50 function items are effectively impossible to pass

findings.evidence: Probe (scratchpad prior_probe.py / cons_probe.py) on the frozen streams skill_rng('knowledge'/'consistency', 'bench'). The subject-blind 'most frequent object of the relation' picker scored: animal_legs 11/16, animal_class 9/16, baby_animal 7/15, vehicle_travel 7/15, shape_sides 4/10. Category score via evals.scoring.normalize: 18.8. The ledger rules only on option-text priors for consistency (Task 16) and on answer ranks for reasoning (Task 11); nothing covers the knowledge answer distribution.
findings.fix: In the bench sampler (knowledge and consistency), stratify by answer. Within each relation, draw the object uniformly (or cap each object at about 1/N_OPTIONS of the relation's items), then a subject with that object. With uniform distractors, the 4-option set is then exchangeable and any subject-blind rule gets exactly 1/4. Add a test that the 'most frequent object' picker stays within about chance + 0.05 on knowledge and consistency. Regenerate before bench-v1 freezes.
findings.line: 46-55 (_sample_facts: uniform over facts within a relation), 68-79 (_bench_pools), 144-164 (knowledge_bench_items), 175 (consistency_groups); kb.py:161-178 (distractors uniform over the other objects)
findings.scenario: Bench facts are drawn uniformly within each relation, so the true answer follows the KB's skewed object counts. The bench pools have mammal at 41% of animal_class, four at 45% of animal_legs, four at 50% of shape_sides, by water at 38% of vehicle_travel and calf at 31% of baby_animal. Distractors are drawn uniformly from the other objects. A model that never learned a single subject fact but picks whichever option is that relation's most common object gets 55/150 MC items (0.367 against chance 0.25) and 5/50 exact items ('four'). With the suite's chance (mean 0.1875 over the 200 items), its knowledge score normalizes to 18.8/100. Over 30 other bench draws the MC rate averages 0.40 (0.35-0.47), so this is systematic, not this seed. An early LM picks up exactly this prior ('...legs does a koala have? Answer: four'), so knowledge reads well above 0 before any fact is known. That breaks R5's 'score 0 at chance' and misleads G3 and the players. consistency_groups uses the same sampler. Its frozen draw happens to sit at chance (0.25), but its expected value is 0.29.
findings.title: Knowledge multiple choice is gameable by each relation's most common answer: a model that ignores the subject scores about 19/100

findings.evidence: The probe tokenizer above splits it into 9 tokens ['ĠB','and','ar','ĠSer','i','ĠB','eg','aw','an']. Every other exact answer is 4 tokens or fewer. The real tok-v1 is trained on more prose and may need 7-9, so this is borderline and unverified without the real tokenizer.
findings.fix: Give knowledge exact items headroom, for example max_new_tokens = max(8, 4 + longest answer length in characters // 2). Or add a build-time check, once tok-v1 exists, that every exact answer fits its budget.
findings.scenario: The frozen knowledge bench has the exact item 'Question: Fill in the blank. The capital city of Brunei is called ___.\nAnswer:' with the only answer 'Bandar Seri Begawan'. Generation stops after 8 tokens, and extract='first_line' then compares the truncated text, for example 'Bandar Seri Begaw'. If tok-v1 needs 9 or more tokens for ' Bandar Seri Begawan', no model can ever pass this item.
findings.title: The knowledge free-answer budget of 8 new tokens may be too short for 'Bandar Seri Begawan', a frozen bench answer

findings.evidence: I read suite.py, types.py, pyproject.toml and grepped every test in scope plus test_bench.py for a golden digest or snapshot of bench items: there is none. Every ledger entry says bench-v1 freezes once players use it.
findings.fix: Add a test that hashes a canonical JSON of build_suite().items (prompts, options, answers, check_args and tags in order) against a recorded digest, with a message that any intended change must bump SUITE_VERSION. Optionally store the digest in the bench report.
findings.scenario: bench-v1 is regenerated in-process from the generator code, the kb_data JSON and numpy Generator streams (choice, permutation, integers). Several things would quietly produce different items still labelled 'bench-v1': a later edit to kb_data (a fact fix in M3), a word added to a generator table, or a numpy upgrade that changes a Generator algorithm (numpy is >=2.5 with no upper bound, and NEP 19 does not promise stream compatibility for Generator). Spec §4.7 keys leaderboards on (bench version, category), so scores from before and after such a change would be silently incomparable. The gate's code digest notices the change for caching, but no test or check ties the label to the content.
findings.title: Nothing pins the bench-v1 item set, so it can change silently under the same version label

findings.scenario: The tokenizer is byte-level BPE with the GPT-2 pre-tokenizer (tokenizer.py:80). The bench prompt ends exactly at that newline, so its last token is a bare 'Ċ'. In all generated code training text, a bare 'Ċ' is never followed by indentation: it is always followed by a column-0 line ('print', 'Output', 'def', ...). Every hidden test fails, and every model reads 0 on all 50 'fmt:function' items. Consequences: coding is capped at about 67, every function-family tag reads 0 for discoveries, and bench-v1 would freeze with this. The gate's G3 needs the code-heavy mix to lead coding by 2 seed-spreads. findings.scenario:
The function prompt is `def f(a, b):
    """doc"""
`. The ByteLevel/GPT-2 pre-tokenizer splits the final "

findings.evidence: I rebuilt the exact conftest tokenizer (byte-identical) and reproduced sharp_lm. Probe th/bf16_margin.py printed step-0 gap 0.014 vs bf16 max logit error 0.218 for 'Once upon a time'. Probe th/bf16_probe.py, using CPU bf16 autocast as a stand-in for CUDA, found the greedy tokens diverge within 10 steps for 10 of 12 sharp-model seeds; seed 1 happens to agree on CPU. Score sums stayed within the test's rel=0.05 (max 0.021), so only the greedy-equality assertion is fragile.
findings.fix: Compare the paths with a tolerance instead of exact argmax equality. For example, teacher-force the CPU greedy sequence through the GPU model and assert the per-step logits agree within about 0.5 (or that the GPU picks the CPU token whenever the fp32 margin exceeds 1.0). Keep the seeded-sampling reproducibility and probability-range checks.
findings.scenario: `test_cuda_bf16_path_tracks_the_cpu_path` uses `sharp_lm` (seed 1, weights x20, 512-vocab fixture tokenizer) and asserts that 10 greedy tokens on CUDA bf16 autocast equal the CPU fp32 tokens. For 'Once upon a time', the fp32 gap between the top two logits at step 0 is 0.014. bf16 changes the logits by about 0.1-0.6, and steps 3, 5 and ('The cat') 4 also have gaps at or below the bf16 error. The test passed on the owner's RTX 3050 during Tasks 5 and 8, but only because the rounding happened to keep the same argmax. Any edit to tests/fixtures/text/*.txt (which retrains the 512-vocab tokenizer and changes the prompt ids), or a torch or cuBLAS change, re-rolls that luck. Then `pytest -m gpu` fails on the owner's machine even though the CUDA path is fine.
findings.title: The GPU test asserts exact greedy-token equality between CPU fp32 and CUDA bf16, but the fp32 top-2 margin (0.014 logits) is far below bf16 rounding error

findings.evidence: Probe th/tagprobe.py runs `run_benchmarks(ScriptedLM(tok), tok, max_items_per_category=10).tag_breakdown()` and prints `{}`. findings.evidence: Decoded every fixture row and counted characters above 127: 0 in all 13 files. Grepped test_build.py, test_corpus.py and test_gate.py: no non-ASCII build input. findings.evidence: Coverage run: trainer.py lines 611 and 618 never execute. grep shows no monkeypatch of rename or PermissionError in test_trainer.py. findings.scenario: The corpus is rebuilt after the judge exists, for example with --retrain-tokenizer after spotting the problem in finding 1, or a full rebuild after Task 15's license or recipe fixes. The local session then runs 'airace-ml build-judge' again, as CLAUDE.md's order suggests. _trained() (judge.py:235-243) compares only the recipe config, so the judge is not retrained. build_judge copies the NEW tokenizer into data/judge/v1 (judge.py:293) next to a model trained on the OLD token ids, recalibrates it and reports success. Judge.load only checks the vocab size (judge.py:102-106), which is 4096 for both. From then on every creativity score and the gate's G2 well-formed check use a judge that reads text through the wrong id mapping, and its calibration percentiles adapt to the garbage, so nothing looks broken. The novelty index has the same gap: its .json records only hash_base, n, sample_mod and count (gate.py:789-795, novelty.py:197-209), never which corpus or tokenizer it indexes. A stale index after a re-tokenize makes almost every window 'new', which inflates creativity. The gate's own runs are keyed by _data_identity (gate.py:721-735), but its judge and index are not checked against it. The only mitigation ('delete data/judge/v1 before build-judge') is written in the SDD ledger alone, not in CLAUDE.md, the build-judge help or the handoff README.
